name: Irrational Procrastination Scale
citation: Steel, 2010. Tracks the intention-action gap — PRD §10.2.
wording_note: Item text below is a good-faith reconstruction of the IPS's themes and is NOT confirmed word-for-word against Steel's original published instrument. Verify against the primary source before this scale is shown to real users — see M2 commit notes.
instructions: How true is each statement of you?

response_scale.label: Neither true nor false of me

items: I put off things so long that my well-being or efficiency unnecessarily suffers.
I delay tasks beyond what is reasonable.
I am continually saying "I'll do it tomorrow."
I put off making decisions until it's too late.
Even tasks that require little else except getting started, I find I get done days later.
I generally delay before starting on work I have to do.
I am not very good at meeting deadlines.
In the back of my mind, I know I should get started, but I still find myself putting it off.
I get things done in time by making myself work earlier than I would like to.
